big_corporate_typical_practice: Automated anniversary tracking across portfolio; portal-generated notices with banked breakdown; applied uniformly on each unit anniversary; compliance staff review before serve
individual_owner_typical_practice: Manual calendar (paper/ spreadsheet); often skip year then bank; relationship-driven; may miss anniversary; less formal documentation
what_is_lawful_ceiling_for_both: Identical: SF Board percentage (now 1.6%) per unit anniversary; one per 12 mo; licensed; 30/90 notice
notes: Corporate efficiency not higher ceiling — practice difference only. Corporate typical observed via industry guides; flagged as practitioner observation not statute.

big_corporate_typical_practice: Centralized ledger of skipped percentages per unit year; additive math verified; banked history exported from Rent Board portal; 90-day triggers flagged by system
individual_owner_typical_practice: Paper memory of skipped years; risk of forfeiting bank by moving anniversary; may lack portal export; bank often unproven if later challenged
what_is_lawful_ceiling_for_both: Same banking rule bankable additive no cap bank must be documented years/amounts + 12 mo elapsed
notes: Same lawful rule both owner types.

big_corporate_typical_practice: Legal team files §37.7/§37.8 petitions centrally; tracks $25k+ competitive bids; amortizes 10-20 years; budgets 10%/$30 cap; hardship stays processed
individual_owner_typical_practice: Less likely to petition; may attempt to pass costs informally without certification (unlawful); less awareness of amortization caps
what_is_lawful_ceiling_for_both: Only certified amortized passthrough enforceable both need Board approval before collection
notes: Secondary flagged; primary Sec 37.7/37.3 but practice claim observational.

big_corporate_typical_practice: Document retention policy 5+ years Notices licenses proofs of service stored digitally; tenant-facing portal log
individual_owner_typical_practice: Less systematic; copies may be email/text; proof of service risk; higher voidance risk if petition filed
what_is_lawful_ceiling_for_both: Same legal retention need — proof required to defend banked amount in petition
notes: Notice requirement same regardless of owner size.

big_corporate_typical_practice: Formal letter on letterhead with Rent Board contact legal citations hardship notice enclosed; multilingual addendum
individual_owner_typical_practice: More personal note may omit required bank breakdown; may include cost narrative not required but lawful if within cap
what_is_lawful_ceiling_for_both: Written dollar/percentage/effective date + banked years required; narrative optional but must not contain threats
notes: Content requirement identical — corporate formality extra but not required.

big_corporate_typical_practice: Standardized written rent-increase policy for all units at same percentage/anniversary; Fair Housing training; disparate-impact review of facial neutral policy
individual_owner_typical_practice: Ad hoc per-unit decisions; may increase one unit not the other based on occupancy tenure without written neutral basis → higher inquiry risk
what_is_lawful_ceiling_for_both: Neutral uniform policy safest under Fair Housing Act and SF anti-harassment §37.10B
notes: Law identical; corporate policy simply more documented — normal business practice distinction.

big_corporate_typical_practice: In-house counsel or panel counsel responds to tenant petitions (Rent Board arbitration) with full chronology; higher settlement rate early
individual_owner_typical_practice: Retained counsel if needed; may default if not respond to Rent Board mediation; free tenant counsel (Tenant Right to Counsel) will still review and can challenge
what_is_lawful_ceiling_for_both: Same standard of review — tenant lawyer applies SF Ordinance not owner size — https://www.sf.gov/information/get-free-legal-help-eviction
notes: Free tenant counsel available against any landlord.

individual_owner_typical_practice: Manual Zillow Rent Calculator or generic not SF-specific → risk wrong percentage (e.g. using AB1482 10% in SF)
what_is_lawful_ceiling_for_both: Must use SF Board official figure not generic calculator; generic mis-states lawful SF cap
